newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt prices off highs, supply fears loom.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt prices off highs, supply fears loom.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices ended the trading day mostly lower and off highs as rumors of the Dart family's repackaging of $1.4 billion in loans to issue structured debt weighed heavily on prices, dealers said.

"The big piece of news this morning was that the Dart family is going to repackage some of their loans as Eurobonds through a trust with the issue expected to yield 100 basis points over a Brady bond," one market source said.
Earlier this year, Brazil reached a debt restructuring deal with the Dart family, the holders of some $1.4 billion of sovereign debt not included in a 1994 Brady accord.
The billionaire Dart family refused to join talks that led to the April 1994 Brady-style debt accord, which restructured $49 billion of Brazilian debt held by private creditors.
In an effort to make their loans liquid the Dart family is expected to issue a little over $1.0 billion in Eurobond debt via Bear Stearns & Co, traders said.

Bradies initially traded off with U.S. Treasuries but were boosted by news that Argentina would price a new global issue only later to suffer a sharp drop when rumors of the Dart family restructuring plan hit the market, traders said.
"Everything was flying...mainly Brazil and Argentina bonds but they traded off their highs when the rumors of the Dart news hit the market," one trader said.
Traders said players feared the new bonds would come in cheaper to some of the bonds currently trading in the market.
"The thinking was that this would force people to sell Bradies in order to buy the issue," said one trader.

Meanwhile, other supply expected to come to market is Argentina's $750 million in 10-year global debt and another $750 million in global debt from Brazil, consisting of five and ten-year maturities, dealers said.
Looking ahead with supply looming in the market, a load of economic indicators coming and the meeting of the International Monetary Fund should make for a very busy week in the market, traders added.
Argentine Pars AR4C23=RR down 3/8 at 58-3/4 bid, while Argentine FRBs ARFLCO5=RR were off 3/8 at 83-3/4.
Meanwhile, Brazilian Cs BR8D14=RR were off 1-1/4 points to trade at 70-1/4 bid and Brazilian Pars BR4D24=RR were down 1/2 at 59-5/8.
In other issues, Russian Vnesh dollar-denominated paper RUVNUSLNS=RR gained 1-1/2 points to trade at a 69-3/4 bid.
Traders said recent positive articles on Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health condition sent debt prices higher.
In the governemnt market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond ended the day off 8/32 at 98-1/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
